retrieved.title: Egypt: the Nile and the natural environment
retrieved.text: Ancient Egyptian life depended on the Nile and its surrounding environment. Fertile land beside the river supplied soil for agriculture. Egyptians distinguished this productive black land from the red land of the surrounding desert. The desert also supplied mineral resources. The Nile therefore helps explain why farming and settlement concentrated along the river rather than across the dry landscape. Archaeologists study objects, written records and images to understand daily life in ancient Egypt.
